result.topic_en: Calculations for a heat-conduction (temperature) problem in an interior bounded by an infinite plane, with coupled diffusion-type equations for u and ρ on two half-lines joined by transition conditions at x=0, solved by exponentially decaying trigonometric solutions.
result.transcription:
Wir haben in der vorigen Stunde [-...-] die Temperatur im Innern eines Körpers unter[?]sucht[?], welcher durch eine unendliche Ebene begrenzt wird
$u+\beta\beta'\varrho$ $\varrho\dots$
$\varrho = e^{\frac{a-x}{\beta'}}\frac{q}{\beta'}$ $u = \text{const} - e^{\frac{a-x}{\beta'}}q$
$m = \frac{q}{\beta'}\int_a^\infty e^{\frac{a-x}{\beta'}}\partial x = \frac{q}{\beta'}$ [-$e^{a-x}$-]
$q = \beta' m$
$\varrho = \frac{m}{\beta'}$ $\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} = -\varrho$
$t>0,\ \alpha\frac{\partial\varrho}{\partial t}+\varrho-\beta\beta\frac{\partial^2\varrho}{\partial x^2}$ $\alpha'\frac{\partial\varrho}{\partial t}+\varrho-\beta\beta'\frac{\partial^2\varrho}{\partial x^2}$ $0<x<\infty,\ t>0$ $x=0\ \Big|\ u+\beta\beta\varrho = u+\beta\beta'\varrho$
$-\infty < x < 0$ $\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+\beta\beta\frac{\partial\varrho}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+\beta\beta'\frac{\partial\varrho}{\partial x}$
$e^{-qt}$ $-\alpha q+1-\beta\beta p p$ $\varrho = e^{-qt}(a\cos\frac{x}{\beta}\sqrt{\alpha q-1}+b\sin\ )$ $e^{-qt}\cos\frac{x}{\beta'}\sqrt{\alpha' q-1}$
$pp = \frac{1-\alpha q}{\beta\beta}$
$p = \frac{i}{\beta}\sqrt{\alpha q-1}$
$\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} = e^{-qt}\frac{\beta}{\sqrt{\alpha q-1}}a\sin\frac{x}{\beta}\sqrt{\alpha q-1} - \frac{b\beta}{\sqrt{\alpha q-1}}\cos\ \ +\varphi t$
$u = e^{-qt}\frac{\beta\beta}{\alpha q-1}(a\cos+b\sin\ ) + \varphi t\, x+\psi t$
$u+\beta\beta\varrho = \beta\beta(\varphi t\, x+\psi t)+\beta\beta\frac{\alpha q-2}{\alpha q-1}(a\cos+b\sin\ )e^{-qt}$
$\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+\beta\beta\frac{\partial\varrho}{\partial x} = \beta\beta\varphi t+\frac{\beta}{\sqrt{\alpha q-1}}(\alpha q-2)(a\sin+b\cos\ )e^{-qt}$

methods.what: Stationary exponential solution for ρ and u with u'' = -ρ
Total quantity m via integral of exponential, giving q = β' m
Diffusion-reaction PDEs on the two half-lines with transition conditions at x=0
Separation of variables with ansatz e^{-qt}, characteristic equation
Integration of u'' = -ρ to get u and the boundary combinations
